Ponderous

PON-duh-ruhs · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Ponderous is heavy, slow-moving, and lacking any grace or liveliness.

The committee's ponderous approval process meant that even simple requests took months to clear.

Worked Example

The old encyclopedia's ponderous, page-long definitions made even simple topics feel like a chore to read.

The writing wasn't just long -- it moved heavily and slowly, without any lightness, which is the clumsy weightiness that ponderous describes.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — ponder

root — ponder: to think about something carefully (from Latin ponderare, 'to weigh') (Latin pondus, 'weight')

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: possessing the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Ponderous shares its root with the verb ponder. Both trace back to Latin pondus, 'weight' -- to ponder is to mentally 'weigh' an idea, while something ponderous is literally or figuratively full of weight: heavy, slow, and graceless.

Use the root in a new word: ponder

Use the root in a new word: ponder: She sat by the window for an hour, pondering whether to accept the job offer.

Word Choice

Ponderous almost always criticizes something for being needlessly heavy, slow, or dull -- a ponderous speech, a ponderous machine, a ponderous style of writing.
